description: Ask the sources again instead of waiting for the next poll: with `incident` (an incident key), re-polls the sources that report its alerts and answers what each alert is now; with `alert` (an alert key such as grafana:1a2b3c4d), the same for one alert; with neither, re-polls every pull source and says how many alerts cleared. At most one poll per source every 10 seconds, so a repeat inside it is answered from the last poll. A pushing sender that takes requests (the regression sweep) is asked to run the check again: each firing alert it reports gets one request, an alert that already has an open one reuses it, and the answer's `pushed[].request` says where it stands (asked, picked up, waiting, ran, failed, cannot, or not picked up within 30 min); a repeat while it is open returns the same request, so it only reads where it stands. Any other pushing sender (webhooks) cannot be forced: the answer says when it last reported, when it reports next if it said, and when the alert clears if it stops sending it. It changes no alert except by the sources' own answers.

by.description: Who is doing this, as "agent: <who>", for example "agent: claude in web-app". Required: it is shown on the tile, in the incident sheet and in History. "agent: " is added when left off. At most 64 characters.

incident.description: An incident key: re-check the alerts that make it up.

name: recheck
title: Re-check now
